INSERT INTO stock_transactions (item_id, transaction_type, quantity, performed_by, notes)
SELECT items.id, 'IN', items.current_stock, users.id, 'Opening balance for demonstration data'
FROM store_items AS items
JOIN users ON users.email = 'stores@psa.local'
WHERE items.current_stock > 0
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM stock_transactions
    WHERE item_id = items.id
      AND notes = 'Opening balance for demonstration data'
);

INSERT INTO maintenance_records (asset_id, issue_description, repair_cost, status, reported_by, service_date)
SELECT assets.id, 'Intermittent startup issue; awaiting technical assessment.', 0.00,
       'Reported', users.id, NULL
FROM assets
JOIN users ON users.email = 'stores@psa.local'
WHERE asset_tag_id = 'PSA-FIN-0001'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM maintenance_records
    WHERE asset_id = assets.id
      AND issue_description = 'Intermittent startup issue; awaiting technical assessment.'
);

INSERT INTO asset_transfers (
    asset_id, from_department_id, to_department_id, requested_by, status
)
SELECT assets.id, source_department.id, destination_department.id, requester.id, 'Pending'
FROM assets
JOIN departments AS source_department ON source_department.code = 'ICT'
JOIN departments AS destination_department ON destination_department.code = 'ADMIN'
JOIN users AS requester ON requester.email = 'admin@psa.local'
WHERE assets.asset_tag_id = 'PSA-ICT-0001'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM asset_transfers
    WHERE asset_id = assets.id
      AND from_department_id = source_department.id
      AND to_department_id = destination_department.id
);

INSERT INTO audit_logs (user_id, action_performed, target_table, record_id)
SELECT users.id, 'Sample asset registered', 'assets', assets.id
FROM assets
JOIN users ON users.email = 'admin@psa.local'
WHERE assets.asset_tag_id = 'PSA-ICT-0001'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM audit_logs
    WHERE action_performed = 'Sample asset registered'
      AND target_table = 'assets'
      AND record_id = assets.id
);

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

require_once __DIR__ . '/../../includes/app.php';
requireRole(['super_admin', 'admin_officer', 'approving_officer', 'management']);

function csvSafeCell(mixed $value): string|int|float|null
{
    if (!is_string($value)) {
        return $value;
    }

    if (preg_match('/^[\x00-\x20]*[=+\-@]/', $value) === 1) {
        return "'" . $value;
    }

    return $value;
}

$typeInput = $_GET['type'] ?? '';
$type = is_string($typeInput) ? trim($typeInput) : '';
$reports = [
    'assets' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-assets.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT assets.asset_tag_id, assets.asset_name, assets.brand, assets.model,
                           assets.serial_number, categories.category_name, departments.department_name,
                           assets.location, assets.condition_status, assets.verification_status,
                           assets.acquisition_date, assets.created_at
                    FROM assets
                    JOIN asset_categories AS categories ON categories.id = assets.category_id
                    JOIN departments ON departments.id = assets.department_id
                    ORDER BY assets.asset_tag_id LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'stock' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-stock-transactions.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT transactions.transaction_date, items.item_name, items.unit,
                           transactions.transaction_type, transactions.quantity,
                           users.full_name AS performed_by, transactions.notes
                    FROM stock_transactions AS transactions
                    JOIN store_items AS items ON items.id = transactions.item_id
                    JOIN users ON users.id = transactions.performed_by
                    ORDER BY transactions.transaction_date DESC, transactions.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'transfers' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-asset-transfers.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT transfers.id, assets.asset_tag_id, source.department_name AS from_department,
                           destination.department_name AS to_department, requester.full_name AS requested_by,
                           approver.full_name AS approved_by, transfers.status, transfers.transfer_date
                    FROM asset_transfers AS transfers
                    JOIN assets ON assets.id = transfers.asset_id
                    JOIN departments AS source ON source.id = transfers.from_department_id
                    JOIN departments AS destination ON destination.id = transfers.to_department_id
                    JOIN users AS requester ON requester.id = transfers.requested_by
                    LEFT JOIN users AS approver ON approver.id = transfers.approved_by
                    ORDER BY transfers.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'maintenance' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-maintenance-records.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT assets.asset_tag_id, assets.asset_name, maintenance.issue_description,
                           maintenance.status, maintenance.repair_cost, reporter.full_name AS reported_by,
                           maintenance.service_date
                    FROM maintenance_records AS maintenance
                    JOIN assets ON assets.id = maintenance.asset_id
                    JOIN users AS reporter ON reporter.id = maintenance.reported_by
                    ORDER BY maintenance.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'audit' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-audit-events.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT logs.`timestamp`, users.full_name AS user_name, users.email,
                           logs.action_performed, logs.target_table, logs.record_id, logs.details
                    FROM audit_logs AS logs
                    LEFT JOIN users ON users.id = logs.user_id
                    ORDER BY logs.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
];

if (!isset($reports[$type])) {
    http_response_code(400);
    exit('Choose a valid report export.');
}

$statement = Database::connection()->query($reports[$type]['query']);
$filename = $reports[$type]['filename'];

header('Content-Type: text/csv; charset=UTF-8');
header('Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="' . $filename . '"');
header('X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff');

$output = fopen('php://output', 'wb');
if ($output === false) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Could not open the report output stream.');
}

fwrite($output, "\xEF\xBB\xBF");
$headersWritten = false;
while ($row = $statement->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC)) {
    if (!$headersWritten) {
        fputcsv($output, array_map('csvSafeCell', array_keys($row)), ',', '"', '');
        $headersWritten = true;
    }
    fputcsv($output, array_map('csvSafeCell', array_values($row)), ',', '"', '');
}

if (!$headersWritten) {
    fputcsv($output, ['No records found'], ',', '"', '');
}

fclose($output);

permissionRequest.newFileContents:
# PSA-SAMS — Initial Operational Release

Public Service Academy Stores and Asset Management System (PSA-SAMS) is a PHP 8 and MySQL/MariaDB application foundation for tracking assets, consumable stores, allocations, maintenance, and audit activity.

## Phase 1 scope

This release includes:

- A relational InnoDB database schema and repeatable demonstration seed data.
- Sign-in, sign-out, CSRF protection, session hardening, password hashing, and five-role access checks.
- An operational dashboard with asset, transfer, stock, maintenance, and recent-activity summaries.
- Asset registration and active assignment/return workflows.
- Asset record maintenance and role-restricted verification status updates.
- Department transfer requests with separate-officer approval and a movement audit trail.
- Store item setup and atomic stock-in/stock-out movements that prevent negative stock.
- Maintenance reporting, status updates, repair costs, and reporting dates.
- Super-administrator user provisioning, account activation/deactivation, and password reset.
- Self-service password changes with account-wide session invalidation and forced password changes for new/reset accounts.
- CSV exports for assets, stock transactions, transfers, maintenance, and audit events, with spreadsheet-formula neutralization.
- Structured JSON details for audited asset, transfer, stock, maintenance, and account-status changes.
- Read-only operational summaries and audit history for permitted oversight roles.
- Responsive role-filtered navigation.

This is an initial operational baseline, not a fully certified deployment. Physical verification evidence (photos/sign-off), formal requisitions, organization-specific approval rules, and tamper-evident audit storage still require implementation and review. Audit events cover implemented actions only; they are application records, not tamper-proof regulatory audit evidence.

## Local setup (XAMPP)

1. Copy this folder to `C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\`.
2. Start Apache and MySQL in the XAMPP Control Panel.
3. Open phpMyAdmin and import `database.sql`. The script creates and selects `psa_sams_db`.
4. Create the first active administrator from a trusted command prompt as described in **Initial administrator** below.
5. Visit `http://localhost/PSA-SAMS/` and sign in with that administrator account.

The local defaults expect MySQL at `127.0.0.1:3306`, database `psa_sams_db`, user `root`, and an empty password. Configure `PSA_DB_HOST`, `PSA_DB_PORT`, `PSA_DB_NAME`, `PSA_DB_USER`, and `PSA_DB_PASSWORD` as environment variables to override those settings. If the application is installed at a different URL path, set `PSA_APP_BASE_URL` (for example, `/my-psa-app`).
`database.sql` is an initial-install script with demonstration records, not a production migration or backup. Import it only into a new/empty environment. Never re-import it over operational records; use reviewed, versioned migrations for future schema changes.

## Demonstration accounts

The SQL file includes five demonstration accounts and sample records. All demonstration accounts are **inactive** and cannot sign in. The shared seed password is for local demonstration only; do not activate or use these accounts with real data.

| Role | Email |
|---|---|
| Super administrator | `superadmin@psa.local` |
| Administration officer | `admin@psa.local` |
| Stores officer | `stores@psa.local` |
| Approving officer | `approver@psa.local` |
| Management (view only) | `management@psa.local` |

The demonstration password hash corresponds to `Password123!`. Demo accounts remain inactive and the seed script does not reset/reactivate existing accounts. If enabling one for a local demo, set a unique password and explicitly mark it active using an administrator-controlled method. Successful logins can update a seeded hash to the current PHP default password algorithm.

## Initial administrator

The first active super administrator must be created from the server command line; the SQL seed does not install an active account with a published password. Use a protected terminal on the database host:

1. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME` and `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` to the authorized operator's details.
2. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` using your organization's approved secret-handling method. Use a unique password of at least 14 characters and at most 72 bytes, with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol. The 72-byte limit avoids bcrypt's input truncation on common PHP installations.
3. From the project directory, run `C:\xampp\php\php.exe bin\create_admin.php` (adjust the PHP path for the managed server).
4. Remove the bootstrap password from the process environment and store it only in the organization's approved password manager.

On Windows PowerShell, you can prompt for the password without putting the value in command history:

```powershell
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME = 'Authorized Administrator'
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL = 'admin@example.org'
$securePassword = Read-Host 'Enter a unique bootstrap password' -AsSecureString
$passwordPointer = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($securePassword)
try {
    $env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($passwordPointer)
    & 'C:\xampp\php\php.exe' 'C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\bin\create_admin.php'
} finally {
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($passwordPointer)
    $securePassword.Dispose()
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME, Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
```

The command refuses to create another initial administrator after an active super administrator exists. The new administrator must change the bootstrap password at first sign-in. Account deactivation and password resets invalidate access on the next protected request. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or 8 hours, whichever comes first. Do not expose bootstrap credentials in shell history, screenshots, support tickets, or source control.

## Security and deployment note

Use XAMPP only for local development and review. Do not expose XAMPP directly to the internet or use this application with real Academy records until the organization has approved a deployment. Operational deployment requires a managed, patched PHP/Apache and MariaDB host on a private network, HTTPS, a dedicated least-privilege database account, secrets management, restricted administration access, tested backups and restores, monitoring, independent security review, and acceptance testing against Academy asset, finance, and approval policies. If a reverse proxy is used, configure authentication rate limits at the trusted edge; the app intentionally does not trust client-supplied forwarding headers. The supplied Apache rules help prevent directory listings and direct access to the SQL seed and configuration directory; verify that Apache allows `.htaccess` overrides in the target environment.
For TLS terminated by a trusted reverse proxy, set `PSA_COOKIE_SECURE=1` in the protected PHP service environment. Do not set it by reading untrusted request headers.

## Project layout

- `auth/` — authentication, session, and access-control helpers.
- `config/` — PDO database connection and Apache access restriction.
- `includes/` — shared application header, role-filtered sidebar, and footer.
- `modules/dashboard/` — Phase 1 operational dashboard.
- `modules/` — dashboard, asset/store workflows, allocations, maintenance, reports, and account management.
- `assets/` — application styles, navigation behavior, and image placeholder.
- `uploads/` — reserved for future verification photos; executable PHP files are denied by the included Apache rule.
- `database.sql` — ten core tables, authentication throttling support, and safe demonstration records.

## Local setup (XAMPP)

1. Copy this folder to `C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\`.
2. Start Apache and MySQL in the XAMPP Control Panel.
3. Open phpMyAdmin and import `database.sql`. The script creates and selects `psa_sams_db`.
4. Create the first active administrator from a trusted command prompt as described in **Initial administrator** below.
5. Visit `http://localhost/PSA-SAMS/` and sign in with that administrator account.

The local defaults expect MySQL at `127.0.0.1:3306`, database `psa_sams_db`, user `root`, and an empty password. Configure `PSA_DB_HOST`, `PSA_DB_PORT`, `PSA_DB_NAME`, `PSA_DB_USER`, and `PSA_DB_PASSWORD` as environment variables to override those settings. If the application is installed at a different URL path, set `PSA_APP_BASE_URL` (for example, `/my-psa-app`).
`database.sql` is an initial-install script with demonstration records, not a production migration or backup. Import it only into a new/empty environment. Never re-import it over operational records; use reviewed, versioned migrations for future schema changes.

## Demonstration accounts

The SQL file includes five demonstration accounts and sample records. All demonstration accounts are **inactive** and cannot sign in. The shared seed password is for local demonstration only; do not activate or use these accounts with real data.

| Role | Email |
|---|---|
| Super administrator | `superadmin@psa.local` |
| Administration officer | `admin@psa.local` |
| Stores officer | `stores@psa.local` |
| Approving officer | `approver@psa.local` |
| Management (view only) | `management@psa.local` |

The demonstration password hash corresponds to `Password123!`. Demo accounts remain inactive and the seed script does not reset/reactivate existing accounts. If enabling one for a local demo, set a unique password and explicitly mark it active using an administrator-controlled method. Successful logins can update a seeded hash to the current PHP default password algorithm.

## Initial administrator

The first active super administrator must be created from the server command line; the SQL seed does not install an active account with a published password. Use a protected terminal on the database host:

1. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME` and `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` to the authorized operator's details.
2. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` using your organization's approved secret-handling method. Use a unique password of at least 14 characters and at most 72 bytes, with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol. The 72-byte limit avoids bcrypt's input truncation on common PHP installations.
3. From the project directory, run `C:\xampp\php\php.exe bin\create_admin.php` (adjust the PHP path for the managed server).
4. Remove the bootstrap password from the process environment and store it only in the organization's approved password manager.

On Windows PowerShell, you can prompt for the password without putting the value in command history:

```powershell
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME = 'Authorized Administrator'
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL = 'admin@example.org'
$securePassword = Read-Host 'Enter a unique bootstrap password' -AsSecureString
$passwordPointer = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($securePassword)
try {
    $env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($passwordPointer)
    & 'C:\xampp\php\php.exe' 'C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\bin\create_admin.php'
} finally {
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($passwordPointer)
    $securePassword.Dispose()
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME, Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
```

The command refuses to create another initial administrator after an active super administrator exists. The new administrator must change the bootstrap password at first sign-in. Account deactivation and password resets invalidate access on the next protected request. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or 8 hours, whichever comes first. Do not expose bootstrap credentials in shell history, screenshots, support tickets, or source control.

## Security and deployment note

Use XAMPP only for local development and review. Do not expose XAMPP directly to the internet or use this application with real Academy records until the organization has approved a deployment. Operational deployment requires a managed, patched PHP/Apache and MariaDB host on a private network, HTTPS, a dedicated least-privilege database account, secrets management, restricted administration access, tested backups and restores, monitoring, independent security review, and acceptance testing against Academy asset, finance, and approval policies. If a reverse proxy is used, configure authentication rate limits at the trusted edge; the app intentionally does not trust client-supplied forwarding headers. The supplied Apache rules help prevent directory listings and direct access to the SQL seed and configuration directory; verify that Apache allows `.htaccess` overrides in the target environment.
For TLS terminated by a trusted reverse proxy, set `PSA_COOKIE_SECURE=1` in the protected PHP service environment. Do not set it by reading untrusted request headers.

## Project layout

- `auth/` — authentication, session, and access-control helpers.
- `config/` — PDO database connection and Apache access restriction.
- `includes/` — shared application header, role-filtered sidebar, and footer.
- `modules/dashboard/` — Phase 1 operational dashboard.
- `modules/` — dashboard, asset/store workflows, allocations, maintenance, reports, and account management.
- `assets/` — application styles, navigation behavior, and image placeholder.
- `uploads/` — reserved for future verification photos; executable PHP files are denied by the included Apache rule.
- `database.sql` — ten core tables, authentication throttling support, and safe demonstration records.

# Deployment handover checklist

This is an operations checklist, not deployment approval. The system owner, ICT, information security, records management, and finance/procurement stakeholders must approve the actual host, retention rules, roles, and workflows before real records are entered.

## Database permissions

1. A DBA creates the database and imports `database.sql` during initial installation.
2. The PHP runtime uses a dedicated account with only `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` on `psa_sams_db`.
3. Keep schema changes and SQL imports under a separately controlled DBA account. The application does not need `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `FILE`, `PROCESS`, or global privileges.
4. `db-grants.sql.example` is a template only. Replace the sample account, host, and secret according to the host's secret policy; do not commit a real credential.

## Application host

- Use a supported PHP release with `pdo_mysql`, a supported patched Apache/PHP handler, and a supported MariaDB/MySQL version.
- Restrict the host and database to approved internal networks; do not expose XAMPP, phpMyAdmin, or MySQL publicly.
- Terminate TLS with organization-managed certificates. If a trusted reverse proxy terminates TLS, set `PSA_COOKIE_SECURE=1` in the protected PHP service environment. Never derive that setting from a client-supplied forwarding header.
- Set database variables (`PSA_DB_HOST`, `PSA_DB_PORT`, `PSA_DB_NAME`, `PSA_DB_USER`, `PSA_DB_PASSWORD`) in protected service configuration, not in the repository.
- Set `PSA_APP_BASE_URL` to the application path. Ensure Apache honors the included access restrictions or reproduce them in the virtual-host configuration.
- Keep `uploads/` non-public. It is denied by `.htaccess`; future file upload/download features need a separately reviewed, authenticated storage service and malware/content validation.
- Restrict file ownership and write permissions. PHP should not be able to modify source code, SQL, or Apache configuration.
- Configure centralized logs, alerting, time synchronization, patching, backup retention, and a documented incident process.
- Take encrypted backups and regularly test full restore, including attachment storage when implemented.

## Release checks

- Import into a new test database and create the initial administrator using the documented CLI bootstrap.
- Verify forced first password change, each role's access boundaries, transfer separation of duties, stock concurrency, reports, and account revocation.
- Run organization-approved security, privacy, accessibility, and user acceptance testing.
- Approve production access and data-retention policies before onboarding users.
- Do not treat application audit rows as tamper-evident records. If formal audit evidence is required, send events to an independently administered, append-only log service.
- The runtime database account should have no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` privilege on `audit_logs`; the example grant file revokes these rights after granting application CRUD elsewhere.

data.reasoningText:
**Finalizing testing protocols**

I'm outlining the final tests, which include accounts, assets, transfers, and reports. My plan involves a careful script with no errors. First, I'll change the initial password and create users for different stores, approvers, and management—up to 72 users. Then, I’ll create an asset register and assign a custodian user. I'll ensure verification is updated and that transfers only happen after all assignments are approved. My testing process looks comprehensive, covering admin login, password changes, and stock receipt checks.

**Planning for asset security tests**

I'm focusing on CSV files for assets, stock, transfers, maintenance, and audit formulas. There’s a potential risk with injection updating the item name formula, which is a concern. I’ll enforce a forced password change on the management login to access reports. Additionally, I'll ensure that any test user with admin rights is forbidden from certain actions to prevent issues. I want to monitor sessions carefully and plan a multi-stage script for admin changes, user role creation, asset handling, and report generation.

<overview>
The user wants the PSA-SAMS PHP/MySQL project advanced toward production quality, after initially asking for a Principal-ready Phase 1 deliverable. The implementation is in the current scratch workspace at `C:\Users\HAWANATU ALLAN\.copilot\chats\6aa9a16a-0feb-4467-93c0-fca8e46e9fb1\PSA-SAMS`; the selected direction was a complete operational baseline for a private managed server, with XAMPP restricted to development/demo. The current work is continuing by adding previously identified features and security controls, then validating a fresh schema and real workflows—without claiming production approval.
</overview>

<history>
1. The user supplied a detailed specification for a PHP 8/MySQL PSA-SAMS system with five roles, ten core tables, authentication, dashboard, and a required directory architecture.
   - Created the initial project in the scratch workspace.
   - Used XAMPP’s PHP binary at `C:\xampp\php\php.exe`; plain `php` was not on PATH.
   - Verified PHP syntax and the seed password hash.

2. The user asked if the work was suitable to present to the Principal and asked for it to be corrected to a high standard.
   - Reviewed and improved setup documentation, seed-data relationships, security defaults, and Apache restrictions.
   - Clarified that the original Phase 1 did not implement full asset, inventory, approvals, maintenance, or reporting workflows.

3. The user requested “production ready,” then said “choose the best.”
   - Chose the broader direction: operational workflows for the five roles, intended for a private managed server—not public XAMPP.
   - Added inactive demo users and a command-line initial-admin bootstrap that forces a password change.
   - Implemented asset registration/edit/verification, assignment/return, transfer requests/approval with separation of duties, stock transactions, maintenance, user administration, reporting, and account password changes.
   - Added login throttling, session expiry/revocation, structured audit details, CSV formula mitigation, restricted uploads, deployment guidance, and least-privilege DB grant template.

4. The user said “continue.”
   - Reviewed existing code and proceeded on remaining identified production gaps: asset editing/verification, self-service password change, exportable reports, richer audit records, and deployment hardening.
   - Found and fixed a CSV-export bug: report `type` was read as POST data even though the endpoint uses GET.
   - Tested end-to-end flows against isolated MariaDB 10.4 and a local PHP server before the most recent audit-schema changes. These included admin bootstrap, forced first password change, stock IN/OUT with insufficient-stock rejection, transfer approval by a separate officer, asset creation/edit/verification, maintenance, user provisioning, management access restrictions, CSV output/formula neutralization, password reset session revocation, and logout.
   - One test initially used the wrong hardcoded user ID when checking password-reset revocation; rerunning with the ID queried by email passed.
   - The latest code added JSON `audit_logs.details` and richer event context. A fresh schema import and final tests were about to be run when compaction interrupted the work.
</history>

<work_done>
Project remains under `C:\Users\HAWANATU ALLAN\.copilot\chats\6aa9a16a-0feb-4467-93c0-fca8e46e9fb1\PSA-SAMS`.

Major files created/changed:
- `database.sql`: 10 core tables plus `login_attempts`; users have `auth_version` and `must_change_password`; audit logs now have a `details JSON` column. Demo accounts are inactive. Seed references departments/users by stable codes/emails, includes assets, stock-opening transactions, maintenance sample, and pending transfer.
- `auth/login.php`, `auth/auth_check.php`, `auth/logout.php`: PDO auth, CSRF, session hardening, authentication throttling with MySQL advisory locks, 30-minute idle/8-hour absolute expiry, status/password-version revocation, forced initial/reset password change, and generic auth failures.
- `bin/create_admin.php`: CLI-only first active administrator setup; unique password policy (14–72 bytes) and one-active-admin guard.
- `includes/app.php`: shared CSRF/form/flash/audit helpers; `recordAudit()` can store JSON before/after details.
- `modules/assets/index.php`: asset registration, edit, verify/unverify actions, validation, transaction locking, audit; department ownership is not editable directly (transfers own that operation).
- `modules/allocation/index.php`: asset assignment/return and transfers; approval requires an approver distinct from requester, asset must still be in source department, not unserviceable, and not actively assigned.
- `modules/stores/index.php`: item creation and atomic stock movements; prevents issues exceeding stock.
- `modules/maintenance/index.php`: issue reports and status/cost/service date updates.
- `modules/users/index.php`: super-admin provisioning, activation/deactivation, reset password; resets require password change and invalidate other sessions via auth version.
- `modules/account/index.php`: current-password-confirmed password changes; increments auth version, preserving current session and revoking others.
- `modules/reports/index.php`, `modules/reports/export.php`: read-only summaries/audit and CSV exports for assets, stock, transfers, maintenance, audit; formula-like strings are prefixed to mitigate spreadsheet formula injection.
- `modules/dashboard/index.php`, `includes/header.php`, `includes/sidebar.php`: operational dashboard, role-filtered navigation, account link.
- `config/db.php`: PDO setup, environment-based DB config including port, generic production error response.
- `assets/css/style.css`: styles for forms, alerts, reports, tables, actions.
- `.htaccess`, `config/.htaccess`, `uploads/.htaccess`: deny indexing/direct DB/config/upload access as configured.
- `README.md`: installation, inactive demo users, forced initial-admin change, scope and non-production caveats.
- `deployment/README.md`, `deployment/db-grants.sql.example`: deployment checklist, least-privilege DB account; example revokes UPDATE/DELETE on audit logs.
- `modules/coming_soon.php` was deleted after all workflows had real entry points.

- All PHP files passed `php -l`.
- Fresh MariaDB 10.4 schema import succeeded (including auth-version/forced-password schema).

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

require_once __DIR__ . '/../../includes/app.php';
requireRole(['super_admin', 'admin_officer', 'approving_officer', 'management']);

function csvSafeCell(mixed $value): string|int|float|null
{
    if (!is_string($value)) {
        return $value;
    }

    if (preg_match('/^[\x00-\x20]*[=+\-@]/', $value) === 1) {
        return "'" . $value;
    }

    return $value;
}

$typeInput = $_GET['type'] ?? '';
$type = is_string($typeInput) ? trim($typeInput) : '';
$reports = [
    'assets' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-assets.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT assets.asset_tag_id, assets.asset_name, assets.brand, assets.model,
                           assets.serial_number, categories.category_name, departments.department_name,
                           assets.location, assets.condition_status, assets.verification_status,
                           assets.acquisition_date, assets.created_at
                    FROM assets
                    JOIN asset_categories AS categories ON categories.id = assets.category_id
                    JOIN departments ON departments.id = assets.department_id
                    ORDER BY assets.asset_tag_id LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'stock' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-stock-transactions.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT transactions.transaction_date, items.item_name, items.unit,
                           transactions.transaction_type, transactions.quantity,
                           users.full_name AS performed_by, transactions.notes
                    FROM stock_transactions AS transactions
                    JOIN store_items AS items ON items.id = transactions.item_id
                    JOIN users ON users.id = transactions.performed_by
                    ORDER BY transactions.transaction_date DESC, transactions.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'transfers' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-asset-transfers.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT transfers.id, assets.asset_tag_id, source.department_name AS from_department,
                           destination.department_name AS to_department, requester.full_name AS requested_by,
                           approver.full_name AS approved_by, transfers.status, transfers.transfer_date
                    FROM asset_transfers AS transfers
                    JOIN assets ON assets.id = transfers.asset_id
                    JOIN departments AS source ON source.id = transfers.from_department_id
                    JOIN departments AS destination ON destination.id = transfers.to_department_id
                    JOIN users AS requester ON requester.id = transfers.requested_by
                    LEFT JOIN users AS approver ON approver.id = transfers.approved_by
                    ORDER BY transfers.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'maintenance' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-maintenance-records.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT assets.asset_tag_id, assets.asset_name, maintenance.issue_description,
                           maintenance.status, maintenance.repair_cost, reporter.full_name AS reported_by,
                           maintenance.service_date
                    FROM maintenance_records AS maintenance
                    JOIN assets ON assets.id = maintenance.asset_id
                    JOIN users AS reporter ON reporter.id = maintenance.reported_by
                    ORDER BY maintenance.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
    'audit' => [
        'filename' => 'psa-audit-events.csv',
        'query' => 'SELECT logs.`timestamp`, users.full_name AS user_name, users.email,
                           logs.action_performed, logs.target_table, logs.record_id, logs.details
                    FROM audit_logs AS logs
                    LEFT JOIN users ON users.id = logs.user_id
                    ORDER BY logs.id DESC LIMIT 5000',
    ],
];

if (!isset($reports[$type])) {
    http_response_code(400);
    exit('Choose a valid report export.');
}

$statement = Database::connection()->query($reports[$type]['query']);
$filename = $reports[$type]['filename'];

header('Content-Type: text/csv; charset=UTF-8');
header('Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="' . $filename . '"');
header('X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff');

$output = fopen('php://output', 'wb');
if ($output === false) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Could not open the report output stream.');
}

fwrite($output, "\xEF\xBB\xBF");
$headersWritten = false;
while ($row = $statement->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC)) {
    if (!$headersWritten) {

result.content:
# PSA-SAMS — Initial Operational Release

Public Service Academy Stores and Asset Management System (PSA-SAMS) is a PHP 8 and MySQL/MariaDB application foundation for tracking assets, consumable stores, allocations, maintenance, and audit activity.

## Phase 1 scope

This release includes:

- A relational InnoDB database schema and repeatable demonstration seed data.
- Sign-in, sign-out, CSRF protection, session hardening, password hashing, and five-role access checks.
- An operational dashboard with asset, transfer, stock, maintenance, and recent-activity summaries.
- Asset registration and active assignment/return workflows.
- Asset record maintenance and role-restricted verification status updates.
- Department transfer requests with separate-officer approval and a movement audit trail.
- Store item setup and atomic stock-in/stock-out movements that prevent negative stock.
- Maintenance reporting, status updates, repair costs, and reporting dates.
- Super-administrator user provisioning, account activation/deactivation, and password reset.
- Self-service password changes with account-wide session invalidation and forced password changes for new/reset accounts.
- CSV exports for assets, stock transactions, transfers, maintenance, and audit events, with spreadsheet-formula neutralization.
- Structured JSON details for audited asset, transfer, stock, maintenance, and account-status changes.
- Read-only operational summaries and audit history for permitted oversight roles.
- Responsive role-filtered navigation.

This is an initial operational baseline, not a fully certified deployment. Physical verification evidence (photos/sign-off), formal requisitions, organization-specific approval rules, and tamper-evident audit storage still require implementation and review. Audit events cover implemented actions only; they are application records, not tamper-proof regulatory audit evidence.

## Local setup (XAMPP)

1. Copy this folder to `C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\`.
2. Start Apache and MySQL in the XAMPP Control Panel.
3. Open phpMyAdmin and import `database.sql`. The script creates and selects `psa_sams_db`.
4. Create the first active administrator from a trusted command prompt as described in **Initial administrator** below.
5. Visit `http://localhost/PSA-SAMS/` and sign in with that administrator account.

The local defaults expect MySQL at `127.0.0.1:3306`, database `psa_sams_db`, user `root`, and an empty password. Configure `PSA_DB_HOST`, `PSA_DB_PORT`, `PSA_DB_NAME`, `PSA_DB_USER`, and `PSA_DB_PASSWORD` as environment variables to override those settings. If the application is installed at a different URL path, set `PSA_APP_BASE_URL` (for example, `/my-psa-app`).
`database.sql` is an initial-install script with demonstration records, not a production migration or backup. Import it only into a new/empty environment. Never re-import it over operational records; use reviewed, versioned migrations for future schema changes.

## Demonstration accounts

The SQL file includes five demonstration accounts and sample records. All demonstration accounts are **inactive** and cannot sign in. The shared seed password is for local demonstration only; do not activate or use these accounts with real data.

| Role | Email |
|---|---|
| Super administrator | `superadmin@psa.local` |
| Administration officer | `admin@psa.local` |
| Stores officer | `stores@psa.local` |
| Approving officer | `approver@psa.local` |
| Management (view only) | `management@psa.local` |

The demonstration password hash corresponds to `Password123!`. Demo accounts remain inactive and the seed script does not reset/reactivate existing accounts. If enabling one for a local demo, set a unique password and explicitly mark it active using an administrator-controlled method. Successful logins can update a seeded hash to the current PHP default password algorithm.

## Initial administrator

The first active super administrator must be created from the server command line; the SQL seed does not install an active account with a published password. Use a protected terminal on the database host:

1. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME` and `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` to the authorized operator's details.
2. Set `PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` using your organization's approved secret-handling method. Use a unique password of at least 14 characters and at most 72 bytes, with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol. The 72-byte limit avoids bcrypt's input truncation on common PHP installations.
3. From the project directory, run `C:\xampp\php\php.exe bin\create_admin.php` (adjust the PHP path for the managed server).
4. Remove the bootstrap password from the process environment and store it only in the organization's approved password manager.

On Windows PowerShell, you can prompt for the password without putting the value in command history:

```powershell
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME = 'Authorized Administrator'
$env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL = 'admin@example.org'
$securePassword = Read-Host 'Enter a unique bootstrap password' -AsSecureString
$passwordPointer = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($securePassword)
try {
    $env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($passwordPointer)
    & 'C:\xampp\php\php.exe' 'C:\xampp\htdocs\PSA-SAMS\bin\create_admin.php'
} finally {
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($passwordPointer)
    $securePassword.Dispose()
    Remove-Item Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_NAME, Env:PSA_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
```

The command refuses to create another initial administrator after an active super administrator exists. The new administrator must change the bootstrap password at first sign-in. Account deactivation and password resets invalidate access on the next protected request. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or 8 hours, whichever comes first. Do not expose bootstrap credentials in shell history, screenshots, support tickets, or source control.

## Security and deployment note

Use XAMPP only for local development and review. Do not expose XAMPP directly to the internet or use this application with real Academy records until the organization has approved a deployment. Operational deployment requires a managed, patched PHP/Apache and MariaDB host on a private network, HTTPS, a dedicated least-privilege database account, secrets management, restricted administration access, tested backups and restores, monitoring, independent security review, and acceptance testing against Academy asset, finance, and approval policies. If a reverse proxy is used, configure authentication rate limits at the trusted edge; the app intentionally does not trust client-supplied forwarding headers. The supplied Apache rules help prevent directory listings and direct access to the SQL seed and configuration directory; verify that Apache allows `.htaccess` overrides in the target environment.
For TLS terminated by a trusted reverse proxy, set `PSA_COOKIE_SECURE=1` in the protected PHP service environment. Do not set it by reading untrusted request headers.

## Project layout

- `auth/` — authentication, session, and access-control helpers.
- `config/` — PDO database connection and Apache access restriction.
- `includes/` — shared application header, role-filtered sidebar, and footer.
- `modules/dashboard/` — Phase 1 operational dashboard.
- `modules/` — dashboard, asset/store workflows, allocations, maintenance, reports, and account management.
- `assets/` — application styles, navigation behavior, and image placeholder.
- `uploads/` — reserved for future verification photos; executable PHP files are denied by the included Apache rule.
- `database.sql` — ten core tables, authentication throttling support, and safe demonstration records.

# Deployment handover checklist

This is an operations checklist, not deployment approval. The system owner, ICT, information security, records management, and finance/procurement stakeholders must approve the actual host, retention rules, roles, and workflows before real records are entered.

## Database permissions

1. A DBA creates the database and imports `database.sql` during initial installation.
2. The PHP runtime uses a dedicated account with only `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` on `psa_sams_db`.
3. Keep schema changes and SQL imports under a separately controlled DBA account. The application does not need `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `FILE`, `PROCESS`, or global privileges.
4. `db-grants.sql.example` is a template only. Replace the sample account, host, and secret according to the host's secret policy; do not commit a real credential.

## Application host

- Use a supported PHP release with `pdo_mysql`, a supported patched Apache/PHP handler, and a supported MariaDB/MySQL version.
- Restrict the host and database to approved internal networks; do not expose XAMPP, phpMyAdmin, or MySQL publicly.
- Terminate TLS with organization-managed certificates. If a trusted reverse proxy terminates TLS, set `PSA_COOKIE_SECURE=1` in the protected PHP service environment. Never derive that setting from a client-supplied forwarding header.
- Set database variables (`PSA_DB_HOST`, `PSA_DB_PORT`, `PSA_DB_NAME`, `PSA_DB_USER`, `PSA_DB_PASSWORD`) in protected service configuration, not in the repository.
- Set `PSA_APP_BASE_URL` to the application path. Ensure Apache honors the included access restrictions or reproduce them in the virtual-host configuration.
- Keep `uploads/` non-public. It is denied by `.htaccess`; future file upload/download features need a separately reviewed, authenticated storage service and malware/content validation.
- Restrict file ownership and write permissions. PHP should not be able to modify source code, SQL, or Apache configuration.
- Configure centralized logs, alerting, time synchronization, patching, backup retention, and a documented incident process.
- Take encrypted backups and regularly test full restore, including attachment storage when implemented.

## Release checks

- Import into a new test database and create the initial administrator using the documented CLI bootstrap.
- Verify forced first password change, each role's access boundaries, transfer separation of duties, stock concurrency, reports, and account revocation.
- Run organization-approved security, privacy, accessibility, and user acceptance testing.
- Approve production access and data-retention policies before onboarding users.
- Do not treat application audit rows as tamper-evident records. If formal audit evidence is required, send events to an independently administered, append-only log service.
- The runtime database account should have no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` privilege on `audit_logs`; the example grant file revokes these rights after granting application CRUD elsewhere.

I need to check the README for mentions of an image placeholder, but what if the actual assets or images aren’t present? I should inspect the directory and see if there's a stale line in the README. There's also something about schema table 11 including audit logs for login attempts, which is good to know. I think I’ll check the PHP runtime settings and run SQL grants in MariaDB to validate everything. I have to remind myself about the project scope too!

**Adjusting SQL grants and verifying assets**

I need to run a grant template in SQL using a random, non-secret password. I’m thinking I can replace it in the command and pipe it to MySQL. If the server is running with `--skip-grant-tables`, that might restrict certain privileges, which is something I need to keep in mind. I’ll also want to inspect the README for the image placeholder and use `Get-ChildItem` for the assets. It’s essential to verify older tests for login throttling too — that’s a priority!

**Assessing potential privilege issues**

I'm noticing a potential production flaw: revoking UPDATE and DELETE privileges on a `database.table` from an app account might inadvertently affect broader database-level privileges. MariaDB does support revoking at the table level, but it seems that privileges at the database level can still persist due to grant configurations. This means that even if I revoke specific table-level access, the broader database privileges might remain intact. I really need to clarify this in the deployment README concerning app grants!

) ENGINE=InnoDB;

    password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    UNIQUE KEY uq_users_email (email),

    KEY idx_users_role_status (role, status),

) ENGINE=InnoDB;

**When to use this tool:**

- Requirements are ambiguous and you need specific, structured input to resolve them

**Choosing field types:**
- **Enum** — when you know likely options (e.g., database engine, auth strategy, log level). The user can still provide a freeform answer. If values are identifiers (snake_case, codes), provide labels via `oneOf: [{const, title}]` so the form is readable.

- **Multi-select array** — when the user may pick any number of values from a known set (e.g., which features to include, which platforms to target). If item values are not human-readable, use `items.anyOf: [{const, title}]` instead of `items.enum`.
- **Number/integer** — for numeric-style configuration (e.g., port, timeout, retry count). The user may still enter freeform text.

- Provide clear `title` and `description` on each field so the user understands what they're choosing
- Set sensible `default` values when a reasonable default exists — if you recommend a specific option, make it the default
- A single-field form is perfectly fine for a simple yes/no or single choice
- Order `properties` keys in the same sequence you discuss the topics in `message` — the form renders fields in property order, so matching the description avoids forcing the user to jump around

**Example — simple single-choice question:**
```json
{
  "message": "What database should I use?",
  "requestedSchema": {
    "properties": {
      "database": {
        "type": "string",
        "title": "Database engine",
        "enum": ["PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "SQLite"],
        "default": "PostgreSQL"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**User actions:**
- The user may **accept** the form (you receive their field values)
- The user may **decline** (they chose not to answer — respect this and proceed with reasonable defaults)
- The user may **cancel** (they want to abort the current interaction)

- Design decisions that significantly affect implementation approach
- Behavioral questions (e.g., "should this be unlimited or capped?")
- Scope ambiguity (e.g., which features to include/exclude)
